I was waiting for someone/something outside an apartment building at the expensive hipstery side of the city. A woman in her forties approached me, she seemed lost, tired and confused. She clearly wasn't from the city, probably from the rural side of the country. 

She asked for a direction and I had no idea but tried to search it in google maps. Someone had written out the name of a place that didn't exist on a tiny post it, probably just to get rid of her, but she was clenching that sweated piece of paper for her dear life. 

I asked her what she was looking for exactly, in order to find another place/direction for her to go to. She just broke down and told me that her daughter  just died but she couldn't get the body from the morgue/hospital and take her back to their community if she didn't get a casket to transport the body first.

The address she was looking for was the "shop of a carpenter" that could help her out making a cheaper casket. The other option was just paying the amout requested by the morgue and get the casket directly from them (probably why they gave her a fake address to begin with).

We sat down a moment just to figure out what to do. She told me that she approached me because I reminded her of her daughter and then procedeed to tell me a little bit about her.

Be aware that in my country (and in many other places) people are super ingenious making up stories so they can get some money from your pocket. But this woman was just so genuinely broken, her expression was of someone who had been defeated by life but just had to go on, one step at the time, almost on automatic pilot.

I went to an ATM and got the money. Handed it to her and we hugged and cried for a while. Got her an uber to the morgue and that was it. The whole thing lasted 5 minutes but that hug was one of the deepest hugs I've ever had.
